## 4.2.0 (HexGhoul): Touka keeps to the café floor; officials stranded on the wrong floor go back; /kagune places says why one is missing

HexKagune 4.2.0 for Forge 1.20.1. Not tested in game. Protocol unchanged (128).

**Version numbers:** you said (quoted exactly): "I keep saying that whenever the version of the mod reaches 9, so like 4.1.9, it passes to
4.2.0. But no, instead look at the version we're already on." You're right, and it was never followed: after 4.1.9 every session went on
to 4.1.10 and up to 4.1.103. From this version on it is x.y.0 to x.y.9, then x.(y+1).0: this is 4.2.0, the next ones 4.2.1 to 4.2.9, then
4.3.0. (4.2.0 still counts as newer than 4.1.103 for Forge and GitHub.) The rule is now in the house rules every session reads first, and
a test fails the build if a version's last number ever passes 9.

**Touka** (you said: she "leaves the front desk of the cafe sometimes to go to a fucking room at the top of her little thing, and she just
stays in the corner"): when she had nothing to do, the game's own stroll picked a random point near her home. "Near" was a ball 4 blocks
round (7 with you about), so the room over the counter was "near": she climbed the stairs, walked to that point (a corner) and stood
there. Now an official's or a companion's stroll at her own place always ends on her own floor (a step or a slab up or down is fine),
and if she is already on another floor (as in your world now) she walks back down to the counter. A married one at the home you share
still roams all of it.

**Officials stranded on the wrong floor:** the same goes for all of them (Banjou in his bedroom upstairs, the General in his office...). A
Banjou from a world made before 4.1.83 stood downstairs (his room was moved upstairs then); if he can't find his way up, he now counts as
out of place, and after a couple of minutes getting no nearer with nobody close enough to see, he is put back in his room (the rule you
gave: never put home in front of you).

**Banjou still not there in your older world:** I couldn't find the cause by reading alone. So `/kagune places`, said in his hideout, now
says for each official why they are or aren't at their spot: every body of theirs loaded and whether it is inside their place, if the
world's record says they're dead (back a day after), married or left waiting somewhere, and how many seconds until they are made at
their spot while you keep their place. Please send me those lines from inside the cottage.
